title: Fidelity Yield Enhanced Equity ETF Review and Aggregate Rating (FYEE)
summary: The Fidelity Yield Enhanced Equity ETF (FYEE) holds an aggregate "Moderate Buy" rating with a consensus price target of $29.02. This rating is based on 758 analyst ratings for 24 companies, which constitute 52.7% of the ETF's portfolio. Top holdings include NVIDIA, Apple, and Microsoft, with NVIDIA showing a potential upside of 53.4%.

title: QQQX: 8%-Plus Yield, 9% Discount, Long-Term NAV Growth (NASDAQ:QQQX)
summary: QQQX is a closed-end fund that generates an 8%+ yield by selling covered calls on NASDAQ 100 stocks, aiming for attractive returns with reduced volatility. The fund boasts a 35% NAV/share increase since inception and currently trades at a 9.11% discount to NAV, providing regular quarterly distributions with potential tax advantages. Despite risks like price volatility and call option risks, QQQX is considered a speculative Buy for investors seeking high yield.

title: The 10 Stocks Hedge Funds Love—and Hate—the Most
summary: Hedge funds are favoring established blue-chip companies like Walmart, Philip Morris International, and Amazon.com, expecting them to continue generating strong returns. Conversely, they are showing disfavor towards clean-energy companies such as Enphase Energy and Albemarle in a volatile market environment. This indicates a shift in investment strategy, prioritizing stable performers over speculative growth in the current economic climate.

title: STMicroelectronics Expands Silicon Photonics
summary: STMicroelectronics has announced advancements in silicon photonics and bipolar CMOS (BiCMOS) technologies to meet the growing demand for high-speed, energy-efficient data transmission in AI and cloud computing. These innovations aim to enable 800Gb/s and 1.6Tb/s optical interconnects with improved power efficiency, with mass production planned for its facility in Crolles, France. The company is collaborating with partners like Amazon Web Services (AWS) to refine its PIC100 silicon photonics platform, positioning itself in a market projected to grow significantly, with silicon photonics anticipated to account for 60% of the optical transceiver market by 2030.

title: 19 Affiliate Marketing Tools to Boost Conversions
summary: This article lists 19 essential affiliate marketing tools to help boost conversions, covering various aspects like SEO, social media management, email marketing, and content creation. Each tool is described with its features, pricing, pros, and cons. The article also provides best practices for choosing and leveraging these tools effectively, emphasizing goal setting, avoiding overlap, and consistency.

title: Dividend Aristocrats In Focus: Walmart Inc.
summary: Walmart Inc. is highlighted as a Dividend Aristocrat and King, having increased its dividend for 52 consecutive years. The company has shown strong growth, particularly in e-commerce, and demonstrated resilience during recessions due to its massive scale and low-cost strategy. Despite its strong performance and strategic investments, the stock is currently considered overvalued, leading to a "hold" rating based on its price-to-earnings ratio and projected total returns.

title: Alphabet’s chief accounting officer sells $238k in stock
summary: Alphabet's Chief Accounting Officer, Amie Thuener O’Toole, sold 1,374 shares of Class C Capital Stock totaling approximately $238,347. This transaction was part of a Rule 10b5-1 Trading Plan. Alphabet maintains strong financial health, with robust cash flows and recent updates in personalized ads policy, AI development, and office attendance requirements for employees.

title: First Class Action Filed Under Washington’s MY Health MY Data Act Draws Parallels to Previous SDK Litigation
summary: The first class action lawsuit under Washington's MY Health MY Data Act (MHMDA) has been filed against Amazon, alleging improper collection and use of consumer location data via Software Development Kits (SDKs). The lawsuit, Maxwell v. Amazon.com, Inc., draws parallels to prior SDK class actions, but introduces MHMDA's broad private right of action for violations related to "consumer health data," which includes precise location information. Businesses are advised to be mindful of SDK use as more states enact privacy legislation and similar lawsuits are expected.

title: AutoZone's Profit Shrinks and Misses Estimates Despite Rising Sales
summary: AutoZone (AZO) reported a year-over-year decline in fiscal second-quarter profit, missing analyst expectations despite an increase in net sales. Net income fell by 5.3% to $487.92 million, or $28.29 per share, while net sales grew by 2% to $3.95 billion, slightly below consensus. The profit decrease was largely attributed to a 6% increase in operating and SG&A expenses and negative foreign currency impacts on international same-store sales.

title: Millennial CEO of Kraft Heinz's most recent acquisition has a hack for being present in meetings—an old-fashioned pink notebook
summary: Verena Zander, the millennial CEO of Just Spices, a Kraft Heinz acquisition, shares her "Good Life" with Fortune, detailing her personal finance habits and work-life balance. Despite the availability of AI tools, Zander prefers an old-fashioned pink notebook for note-taking in meetings, believing it fosters better presence and memory retention. The article also touches on the growth of Just Spices under her leadership and offers insights into her daily routines and investment choices.

title: Kornit Apollo for American Classics Apparel
summary: American Classics Apparel, a major wholesaler of licensed music, film, and gaming apparel, has adopted the Kornit Apollo platform to transition from traditional screen printing to high-speed digital production. This move is aimed at meeting increasing customer demand and leveraging the expanding e-tailer marketplace. The integration of Kornit Apollo will enhance the company's speed, efficiency, and quality in delivering licensed apparel.

title: Pardon the Disruption: Where does Kroger go from here?
summary: Rodney McMullen's unexpected resignation as Kroger CEO leaves the supermarket giant facing significant challenges, including stiff competition from discounters, an uncertain omnichannel strategy, and the failed Albertsons merger. The new CEO will need to innovate and revitalize Kroger's core grocery business, digital presence, and explore further acquisitions to maintain relevance in a rapidly evolving market. Despite its strengths in private label and alternative profit streams, Kroger must adapt to customer demands and differentiate itself beyond traditional supermarket advantages.

title: Philips just launched its first Roku OLED TV and it looks like a steal for PS5 owners
summary: Philips has introduced its first Roku OLED TV, the 65-inch Class 974 Series, which offers a 4K 120Hz refresh rate for $1,299. This model is presented as a cost-effective option for PS5 owners, providing premium gaming features at a lower price point than comparable LG or Sony OLED TVs, though it is currently exclusive to Sam's Club members. The TV includes Dolby Vision IQ, HDR10, Dolby Atmos, and AMD FreeSync Premium, making it a strong contender in the gaming TV market.

title: CISO Global Continues to Advance AI-Powered Security Solutions within Microsoft and Amazon Cloud
summary: CISO Global is advancing its AI-powered security solutions within Microsoft Azure and Amazon AWS ecosystems. The company successfully developed a Proof of Concept for integrating its Argo Secure platform with Microsoft Security Copilot, enhancing asset management and threat detection. Additionally, CISO Global's TIGRIS GRC solution is now available on the AWS Marketplace, offering cloud-based security assessment and compliance tools.

title: Armlogi Holding Corp. Announces Letter of Intent to Acquire Leopard Transnational Inc.
summary: Armlogi Holding Corp. (Nasdaq: BTOC) has announced a non-binding Letter of Intent to acquire Leopard Transnational Inc., a California-based logistics provider. This strategic acquisition aims to expand Armlogi's warehousing footprint by 360,000 square feet and enhance its e-commerce fulfillment capabilities, particularly benefiting cross-border e-commerce sellers and major online marketplaces. The deal, which involves Armlogi common stock and potential earn-out payments, is expected to be finalized within 60-90 days, pending due diligence and necessary approvals.

title: What Is Direct Indexing?
summary: Direct indexing allows investors to own the individual stocks within an index directly, offering benefits like tax-loss harvesting and customizability for ESG or other preferences. However, it is most suitable for those with substantial taxable investments due to potential complexities, higher fees, and the risks associated with active management and tracking error. The strategy can enhance tax efficiency and align portfolios with personal values but requires significant oversight and may not always outperform traditional index funds.

title: Polar announces new AI-ready data center powered by 100 percent renewable energy in Norway
summary: Polar has announced the construction of a new multi-phase, AI-ready data center in Tørdal, Norway, powered entirely by renewable hydroelectric energy. The first phase, DRA01, will provide 12MW of capacity and is expected to be operational in the second half of 2025, addressing the increasing demand for AI computing infrastructure in Europe. The facility leverages Norway's natural resources for energy efficiency and features advanced liquid cooling and high-density rack configurations optimized for AI applications.

title: Salesforce joins growing list of companies ending diversity hiring initiatives
summary: Salesforce Inc. has become the latest company to end its diversity hiring initiatives, removing language about diversity and inclusion from its annual financial disclosure. This decision follows executive orders signed by President Donald Trump targeting the elimination of DEI programs. Other major companies like Google, Meta, Target, Amazon, Walmart, and Deloitte have also rolled back similar initiatives.

title: Why Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd (CRDO) Went Down on Wednesday
summary: Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd (CRDO) stock fell by 13.97 percent on Wednesday despite reporting impressive third-quarter fiscal year 2025 earnings. The decline is attributed to investors having already factored in higher income due to the company's growth in AI infrastructure and strong customer base, including Amazon, Tesla, and Microsoft. While CRDO posted significant increases in net income and revenues, it was among the worst performers for the day, suggesting that some AI stocks may offer more promising returns.

title: Arlo Essential XL Outdoor Security Camera, Tested: The Best Overall Model You Can Buy
summary: This article reviews the Arlo Essential XL Outdoor Security Camera, highlighting its impressive battery life, ease of setup, and solid performance without requiring a monthly subscription for basic features. Priced at $150, it offers 2K resolution, color night vision, and an integrated spotlight, setting it apart from competitors. While advanced features necessitate a subscription, the camera's core functionality makes it a top recommendation for both renters and homeowners.

title: Legislature takes up plan to shield Oregon consumers from data centers’ power costs
summary: Oregon lawmakers are considering House Bill 3546 to protect residential consumers from the rising costs of powering data centers. The bill would classify data centers and cryptocurrency miners as a new utility customer class, giving regulators authority to ensure households and small businesses don't shoulder these costs, and requiring new high-load customers to sign 10-year power purchase contracts. While some tech companies like Google support the idea of multi-year agreements and infrastructure charges, they suggest expanding the bill to cover all large power loads, not just data centers, and including collateral requirements.

title: Grayscale Investments LLC Grayscale Zcash Trust (ZEC) (ZCSH) reports earnings
summary: Grayscale Investments LLC Grayscale Zcash Trust (ZEC) (ZCSH) has filed its annual 10-K report for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024. The Trust aims to track the value of ZEC, holding approximately 2.4% of ZEC in circulation as of year-end, and the report details its operations, risks associated with digital assets, and the role of Grayscale Investments LLC as the Sponsor.

title: Defined Outcome ETFs: Good For Conservative Investors, Not Necessarily Conservative Investments
summary: Defined Outcome ETFs utilize options to provide a buffer against downside risk while capping potential upside, making them appealing to conservative investors. This article argues that these strategies are particularly effective when applied to volatile markets like China's internet sector, where they can offer higher upside potential compared to similar strategies for more stable assets such as the S&P 500 Index. The KraneShares 100% KWEB Defined Outcome January 2027 ETF (KPRO) and the KraneShares 90% KWEB Defined Outcome January 2027 ETF (KBUF) are highlighted as examples that apply this strategy to the volatile but high-growth China internet sector.

title: The Friday Checkout: Exits of Kroger and Albertsons chiefs tell a tale of two grocers
summary: The CEOs of Kroger and Albertsons, Rodney McMullen and Vivek Sankaran, have both departed their companies after their attempted merger failed due to regulatory issues. Kroger, under new leadership, is projecting growth and investing in new stores, while Albertsons is implementing aggressive cost-cutting measures, including store closures and layoffs, as it seeks stability with a new CEO. This column also covers other grocery industry news, including Uber Eats' partnership with FreshDirect, Arkansas's proposed grocery tax elimination, Kroger's foot traffic data, and Aldi's new fan gear for kids.

title: Downtown Seattle mainstay closing soon
summary: The Cheesecake Factory's downtown Seattle location, operating for over two decades, will close on May 4 due to an extensive company review. This closure, along with other national brands departing, signifies another challenge for downtown Seattle's revitalization efforts following the pandemic. Despite some new developments and recommitments, the area continues to face setbacks in commercial activity.

title: The Case for Costco Stock Hitting $1,000 in the Next Year
summary: Costco (COST) stock has significantly outperformed the broader market, even with its high valuation and a recent dip from an all-time high of $1,078.23. Analysts are optimistic about its future, with one setting a price target of $1,205, driven by the company's strong business model, loyal customer base, and investments in e-commerce and recent membership fee hikes. While there are concerns about its high P/E ratio, its consistent growth and strong earnings performance are seen as justifying its premium.

title: After Earnings, Is Salesforce Stock a Buy, a Sell, or Fairly Valued?
summary: Salesforce CRM recently released its fourth-quarter earnings, showing results generally in line with expectations, supported by healthy multi-cloud deals and an expanding AI platform. Morningstar maintains a fair value estimate of $315.00 per share, rating the stock as ★★★ (fairly valued) with a wide economic moat and high uncertainty. The company's financial strength is considered sound, with a solid net cash position and growing margins, despite risks related to leadership and revenue growth deceleration in certain segments.

title: Congressman Ditches Russell 2000 ETF To Buy Lithium, Uranium ETFs
summary: Senator John Boozman (R-Ark.) recently sold his position in a Russell 2000 ETF and purchased Sprott Lithium Miners ETF and Sprott Uranium Miners ETF. This move suggests a belief that these commodities may outperform the broader stock market. Boozman has shown previous interest in Arkansas' lithium production and the U.S.'s role in energy independence, potentially influenced by trade policies.

title: News | Tech CEO follows his customers in relocating to South Florida
summary: Varonis, a technology company, is relocating its headquarters from New York to Miami, following a trend of businesses moving to South Florida. Co-founder and CEO Yaki Faitelson cited Miami's business-friendly environment, quality of life, and ability to attract talent and clients as key factors. The move reflects Miami's growing appeal as a hub for finance, tech, and professional services, though the local office market is currently experiencing a moderation after a pandemic-era boom.

title: Coinbase to Debut Combined Equities & Crypto Index Futures
summary: Coinbase Derivatives is set to launch Mag7 + Crypto Equity Index Futures on September 22, offering the first US-listed derivative that provides combined exposure to traditional equities and cryptocurrency ETFs. This innovative product aims to provide thematic exposure to innovation and growth assets, diversification, and strategic risk management. The index will include the "Magnificent 7" stocks (AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, NVDA, META, TSLA), Coinbase Global Inc. (COIN), and cryptocurrency ETFs (IBIT, ETHA), with an even-weighting methodology and quarterly rebalancing.

title: Netgear Orbi 870 Wi-Fi 7 mesh router review: Solid performance can’t mask high price and feature regression
summary: The Netgear Orbi 870 Wi-Fi 7 mesh router delivers solid wireless performance across 6 GHz and 5 GHz bands but falls short on features compared to competitors and its more expensive sibling, the Orbi 970. Despite its high price of $1,299 for a three-node system, it lacks 5 Gbps or 10 Gbps LAN ports and USB connectivity, which are available on similarly priced or even cheaper alternatives. Reviewer Brandon Hill criticizes the Orbi 870's value proposition, suggesting that other mesh systems offer comparable performance with better hardware and software capabilities for the same or less cost.

title: Whole Foods at The Shops at Sun Vet to open earlier than planned, developer says
summary: The Shops at SunVet in Holbrook, formerly Sun Vet Mall, is over 70% leased and on track for completion this year, with Whole Foods Market opening earlier than expected in fall 2025 instead of spring 2026. This $93 million redevelopment by Regency Centers Corp. is transforming the struggling 1970s mall into an upscale open-air shopping center with tenants like Nordstrom Rack, Shake Shack, and Sephora. Mild winter weather allowed for accelerated construction, contributing to the earlier opening of Whole Foods.

title: ARM & HAMMER™ Laundry and Meghan Trainor Hit All the Right Notes with the 'Toss Like This' Laundry ‘Re-Trainor’ Campaign!
summary: ARM & HAMMER Laundry has partnered with GRAMMY® winning artist Meghan Trainor for a campaign called “Toss Like This,” aimed at simplifying laundry routines with ARM & HAMMER POWER SHEETS™ Laundry Detergent. Trainor transforms her hit song into a playful jingle to highlight the convenience and eco-friendliness of the new detergent sheets, which eliminate bulky plastic bottles and offer powerful cleaning. The POWER SHEETS are available on Amazon and Walmart, packaged in recyclable cartons and designed for easy use at home or on the go.

title: Arkansas Faces Surge in Power Demand from AI & Data Centers
summary: Arkansas and national utility leaders are preparing for a significant increase in electricity demand driven by AI hubs, data centers, and other power-intensive industries. This surge could lead to higher electricity bills but also presents an opportunity for economic development, with utilities seeking legislation to finance new power plants and attract large projects like Elon Musk's xAI data center. The article highlights the scale of this projected demand growth, with Arkansas Electric Cooperative Corp. already evaluating requests for 4,000 megawatts of additional load, and utility companies like AECC and Entergy Arkansas are planning new natural gas-fired generation plants to meet future needs and replace retiring coal plants.

title: Exclusive: How NetApp is navigating the fourth wave of technology with AI-driven data infrastructure
summary: NetApp's Chief Technology Evangelist, Matt Watts, discusses how the company is adapting to the "fourth wave" of technology driven by intelligent data infrastructure and AI, learning from past technological shifts like virtualization and cloud adoption. The article highlights NetApp's unified storage and intelligent services as key solutions for AI integration, addressing challenges such as data silos and security, while also predicting quantum computing as the potential "fifth wave." Watts emphasizes the importance of letting go of outdated systems and embracing change to stay innovative.

title: Palantir (NASDAQ:PLTR) Extends Collapse as Tech Stock Carnage Exposes Giant Valuation Gap
summary: Palantir (PLTR) stock has experienced a significant collapse, losing over a third of its market cap in three weeks, despite its upcoming inclusion in the S&P 100. This downturn is attributed to a broader tech stock selloff, concerns over potential defense spending cuts by the U.S. government—a major client for Palantir—and the exposure of previously lofty valuations in the tech sector. Analysts currently rate PLTR as a Hold, with an average price target suggesting a 20% upside.

title: Ulta Beauty’s new CMO on balancing cultural pizzazz with socially minded initiatives
summary: Ulta Beauty's new CMO, Kelly Mahoney, discusses the brand's strategy of blending high-profile cultural marketing, such as Super Bowl and Golden Globes sponsorships, with a continued commitment to DEI initiatives and customer accessibility. Mahoney emphasizes the importance of authentic social media engagement and the strategic balance required to navigate economic uncertainties like tariffs while maintaining brand relevance and purpose.

title: Vodafone: Be in the office 8 days a month or lose bonuses
summary: Vodafone is mandating its UK employees to work in the office at least eight days a month, or face disciplinary action and potential loss of bonuses starting April 1. This policy, in place since 2021, is now being strictly enforced, despite staff concerns about reduced office space and the need to collaborate with remote international teams via video calls. The company emphasizes the importance of in-office collaboration while employees point to research questioning the productivity benefits of RTO mandates and the impact on morale.

title: Why FCF ETF 'VFLO' Looks Strong in 2025
summary: The VictoryShares Free Cash Flow ETF (VFLO) demonstrated strong demand in 2024 and is well-positioned for 2025, offering diversification, attractive valuations, and strong historical returns. VFLO targets large-cap U.S. companies with high free cash flow yields, excluding "Magnificent Seven" stocks, making it a valuable complement to broad benchmarks. Its performance in 2024, generating a nearly 22% return, highlights its potential to improve value exposure in portfolios.

title: Oracle misses on earnings and issues weak revenue guidance
summary: Oracle reported fiscal third-quarter results that fell short of analysts' expectations for both earnings and revenue, and issued weak revenue guidance for the current quarter. Despite this, the company's cloud infrastructure unit continued to see strong growth due to AI demand, with revenue up 49% from the previous year. Oracle also announced an increase in its quarterly dividend to 50 cents a share.

title: Is It Time to Buy the Magnificent Seven?
summary: After a recent selloff in the US stock market, the valuations of the "Magnificent Seven" mega-cap tech stocks have decreased. Morningstar analysts now consider Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet to be undervalued, while Nvidia and Tesla are fairly valued, and Apple remains overvalued. Despite these changes, Morningstar strategists continue to recommend underweighting growth stocks, favoring a rotation into value stocks.

title: Live Nation: Total tickets sold by Ticketmaster annually (2010-2024)
summary: This article examines the annual number of tickets sold by Ticketmaster, a Live Nation Entertainment platform, from 2010 to 2024. It details how Live Nation reports these figures in its financial updates, including both primary and secondary, fee-bearing and non-fee-bearing tickets. The data visualization is based on this information, offering insights into Ticketmaster's sales volume over the years.

title: Druva debuts fully integrated support for Microsoft Azure
summary: Druva, a SaaS platform for data security and backup, has introduced integrated support for Microsoft Azure, expanding its services beyond its decade-long AWS exclusivity. This move allows Druva customers to backup Microsoft Azure and Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud VMs to Azure Storage, with further services planned through a strategic partnership with Microsoft. The development addresses the growing multi-cloud environment used by enterprises and positions Druva to meet broader market demands.

title: UNFI sees sales rise as efficiency improves
summary: United Natural Foods, Inc. (UNFI) reported a nearly 5% year-over-year rise in net sales to $8.2 billion in Q2 fiscal 2025, driven by its natural products business, while narrowing its net loss to $3 million. The company's wholesale operations saw an increase in adjusted EBITDA, while the retail division experienced a slight decline due to store closures, though identical store sales largely improved. UNFI also focused on efficiency, improving safety, delivery quality, and productivity at its facilities, and plans to use proceeds from distribution center sales to reduce debt.

title: $120M TowneBank-Village Bank acquisition approved by state, FDIC
summary: TowneBank's $120 million acquisition of Midlothian’s Village Bank and Trust Financial Corp. has received approval from the FDIC and the Virginia State Corporation Commission. This clearance paves the way for the deal to be completed in early April. The combined entity will operate under the TowneBank name, boasting approximately $17.8 billion in assets and incorporating Village Bank's nine branch offices into its network.

title: Board Approves Termination of Investment Sub-Advisory Agreement for First Trust TCW Securitized Plus ETF
summary: First Trust Advisors L.P. announced that the Board of Trustees of First Trust Exchange-Traded Fund VIII voted to terminate the investment sub-advisory agreement for the First Trust TCW Securitized Plus ETF, effective May 9, 2025. First Trust Advisors L.P. will assume portfolio management responsibilities for the Fund, maintaining existing investment strategies. The company, along with its affiliate First Trust Portfolios L.P., manages approximately $266 billion in collective assets.

title: Bank of America stock hits 52-week high at 53.64 USD
summary: Bank of America's stock reached a 52-week high of $53.64, driven by a 29.71% increase over the past year and strong investor confidence. This performance follows a solid third-quarter revenue report and increased adoption of its AI-powered financial tools. The bank also made significant executive appointments and its analysts commented on market-influencing investment deals.

title: Tech Moves: Longtime Google leader Umesh Shankar joins Microsoft as new corporate VP
summary: Umesh Shankar, a veteran leader from Google, has joined Microsoft AI as a corporate vice president of engineering, focusing on privacy and security for the Copilot AI assistant. This move is part of a trend of Google executives moving to Microsoft AI. The article also details other significant personnel changes at Remitly, Crelate, Bloomberg, Pioneer Square Labs, Seattle Aquarium, Built Oregon, Fred Hutch Cancer Center, and Trove.

title: Is it time to buy the Magnificent Seven?
summary: The "Magnificent Seven" tech stocks have experienced a significant selloff, making some of them appear undervalued according to Morningstar's fair value metrics. While Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet are now rated as buys, Nvidia and Tesla are fairly valued, and Apple remains overvalued. Morningstar strategists still recommend underweighting growth stocks overall, favoring value stocks due to market volatility and slowing economic growth.

title: The maker of Roomba has ‘substantial doubt’ about surviving
summary: iRobot, the maker of Roomba, has expressed "substantial doubt" about its ability to continue as a company, according to its latest quarterly earnings report. This dire warning follows the collapse of a planned $1.7 billion acquisition by Amazon due to regulatory concerns. The company's stock plummeted 30% in premarket trading, and its board is now exploring strategic alternatives amidst mounting debt.

title: FEPI Stock Fund Price and Chart — NASDAQ:FEPI
summary: This article provides an overview of the REX FANG & Innovation Equity Premium Income ETF (FEPI), detailing its price performance, key statistics like AUM and dividend yield, and investment strategy. FEPI employs a covered call strategy on top US technology companies, aiming for income generation and limited capital appreciation. The fund's historical performance, asset allocation, and technical analysis indicators are also presented.

title: CVS SWOT Analysis (2025)
summary: This article provides a comprehensive SWOT analysis of CVS for the year 2025, detailing its strengths such as reliable suppliers, large scale, and strong brand name, alongside weaknesses like inventory management and high staff turnover. It also identifies opportunities in technology investment, online channels, and diversification through acquisitions, while highlighting threats from local distributors, regulation risks, and inflation. The analysis evaluates CVS's current market position and potential future challenges and growth areas.

title: Fossil Group names new CFO
summary: Fossil Group has appointed Randy Greben as its new chief financial officer, effective March 17. Greben will be responsible for overseeing the company's global financial strategy, with a focus on its financial turnaround and business transformation. He brings over two decades of financial leadership experience from companies like Casper Sleep, Blue Apron, and Ann Inc.

title: Fossil leans on layoffs, more store closures to cut costs
summary: Fossil Group is implementing layoffs and closing approximately 50 more stores to save $100 million in selling, general, and administrative expenses after a Q4 net sales plunge of nearly 19%. The company aims to shift its focus towards its wholesale channel and make its direct-to-consumer business smaller but more profitable. Former Casper CFO Randy Greben has been hired as the new CFO to help lead these business transformations and turnarounds.

title: E-Commerce Automotive Aftermarket Size, Share | CAGR of 22.4%
summary: The global E-Commerce Automotive Aftermarket is projected to grow from USD 67.4 Billion in 2024 to USD 508.7 Billion by 2034, exhibiting a CAGR of 22.4%. This growth is driven by digitalization, increasing vehicle ownership, and consumer preference for online shopping, with North America currently dominating the market. Key trends include AI-powered recommendations, mobile-friendly platforms, omnichannel strategies, and the emergence of eco-friendly auto parts.

title: Target engages in grocery war by arming supply chain
summary: Target is enhancing its food supply chain by increasing its temperature-controlled food distribution centers from nine to ten, aiming to ensure products remain in stock during peak shopping periods. This strategic move is part of Target's effort to compete with grocery giants like Walmart and Amazon, despite recent struggles in overall earnings. The retailer also plans to focus on offering a wider assortment of goods and faster delivery services to consumers, building on its $6.5 billion in food and beverage sales in the first quarter, which saw low single-digit growth.

title: Starbucks CEO defends company's diversity, says they are 'key' strength of business
summary: Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol emphasized at a recent shareholder meeting that diversity remains a core strength for the company. Despite other corporations scaling back on diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) initiatives, Niccol asserted that reflecting the diversity of customers and staff globally is crucial for Starbucks, which operates 40,000 stores in 88 markets. He added that a diverse board of directors is also vital for the company's success.

title: Roomba maker says 'substantial doubt' about future of company
summary: iRobot, the company behind Roomba vacuums, has issued a warning of "substantial doubt" about its ability to continue as a going concern, citing a significant revenue decrease and annual net loss in fiscal 2024. The company is evaluating a "broad range of alternatives" for its business, including debt refinancing and transactions, after facing aggressive competition and the termination of a proposed acquisition by Amazon. These challenges come even as iRobot launched new robot vacuum models and implemented an operational restructuring to focus on profitability.

title: Oracle Mission Statement | Sustainability Goals | Core Values | Strategy (2025 Analysis)
summary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of Oracle's mission statement, corporate responsibility, sustainability goals, and core values as of 2025. It details how Oracle aims to help customers manage and leverage data, promote technological freedom, and contribute to a sustainable environment through various initiatives and its commitment to values like integrity, customer satisfaction, and teamwork. The article also provides key financial and company information for Oracle.

title: Stock Market Today: Dow Sinks 537 Points On Tariff Threats As S&P 500 Corrects; Gold Miners Jump, Meta Triggers Sell Rule (Live Coverage)
summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 537 points, and the S&P 500 corrected amid new tariff threats from the Trump administration. Gold miners rallied while Home Depot and Meta Platforms experienced sell-offs, with Meta triggering a sell rule. Despite a late attempt by traders to cover short positions, major indexes ended the trading day lower.

title: Applied Optoelectronics Soars Following Share Purchase Agreement With Amazon
summary: Shares of Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI) are experiencing a significant surge, climbing over 35 percent, following the announcement of a share purchase agreement with Amazon. Amazon.com, Inc. has been issued a warrant to acquire approximately 8 million shares, as disclosed in a recent SEC filing. This news has led to a boost in AAOI's stock price, which traded at $21.60 on Friday morning.

title: GE Vernova, Amazon Expand Effort to Address Surge in Global Energy Demand
summary: GE Vernova and Amazon Web Services (AWS) are expanding their collaboration to address rising global energy demand and advance decarbonization goals. GE Vernova will provide essential electrical equipment and construction support to AWS for its data center expansion, while also working on onshore wind development projects. AWS, in turn, will offer cloud services to GE Vernova, aiding its cloud migration, digital innovation, and the use of generative AI to optimize operations and accelerate technology development.

title: ETF Spotlight: XLY Plunges With Consumer Sentiment
summary: The Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLY) has been a poor performer in 2025 due to declining consumer sentiment, triggered by economic uncertainty, inflation fears, and a trade war. Despite short-term struggles, the article suggests this downturn could be a buying opportunity for long-term investors, as consumer spending tends to rebound. XLY, heavily weighted with Amazon and Tesla, offers exposure to leading consumer brands but carries risks like cyclicality and concentration.

title: Five Investment Themes to Watch in Equity and Alternative for 2025
summary: In 2025, investors are focusing on diversification and risk management due to shifting macroeconomic conditions, a new U.S. administration, and evolving trade policies. Key investment themes include diversifying within U.S. equities, increasing exposure to international equities, particularly in Japan, and utilizing commodities and cryptocurrencies for portfolio diversification and inflation hedging. The article highlights the role of CME Group's various futures and options contracts in managing these investment strategies.

title: Summit Therapeutics (SMMT) reports inducement grants
summary: Summit Therapeutics (SMMT) announced the grant of inducement awards consisting of options to purchase 122,650 shares of common stock to 12 new employees. These awards, granted on March 11, 2025, have an exercise price of $18.50 per share and vest in equal annual installments over four years. The grants were made to attract new employees, in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4).

title: NEOS Nasdaq-100 Hedged Equity Income ETF Review and Aggregate Rating (QQQH)
summary: The NEOS Nasdaq-100 Hedged Equity Income ETF (QQQH) has an aggregate rating of "Moderate Buy" based on analysis of its holdings. MarketBeat calculates this rating and a price target by considering Wall Street analyst ratings for the individual stocks within the ETF's portfolio. The aggregate price target for QQQH is $53.32, with its top holdings including NVIDIA, Apple, Microsoft, and Amazon.com.

title: Western Digital unveils 26TB 3.5-inch Red Pro SATA NAS HDD
summary: Western Digital has launched a new 26TB 3.5-inch WD Red Pro hard drive (WD260KFGX) designed for network-attached storage (NAS) devices. This new drive uses conventional magnetic recording (CMR) technology, offering high capacity and reliability with a 2.5-million-hour mean time between failure (MTBF) rating and 550 TB per year of data transfers. It is priced at $569.99 and is optimized for demanding, always-on NAS usage, including RAID settings, with anti-vibration technology and OptiNAND.

title: My Health, My Dollar: Amazon’s Health Data Troubles in Washington
summary: Amazon is facing a first-of-its-kind lawsuit under Washington’s My Health My Data Act (MHMDA), alleging unauthorized collection and monetization of health-related data through its SDKs without user consent. The case highlights the MHMDA's strict requirements, which go beyond HIPAA, and its provision for a private right of action. This legal challenge underscores the increasing scrutiny on companies handling consumer health information and necessitates a re-evaluation of data privacy practices to align with evolving legal landscapes.

title: OUTtv Makes Historic Move Into Asian Market With Taiwan Launch
summary: OUTtv, a leading LGBTQ+ television and streaming service, is expanding its reach into Asia with a historic launch in Taiwan through a partnership with Chunghwa Telecom. This move marks OUTtv's first entry into the Asian market, building on recent growth in New Zealand and Nordic countries. The collaboration aims to provide diverse and authentic LGBTQ+ storytelling to a new audience, leveraging Chunghwa Telecom's extensive subscriber base.

title: I tested the Traeger Woodridge Pro, and it's ideal for set-it-and-forget-it smoking
summary: The Traeger Woodridge Pro is a hybrid pellet grill that excels at smoking, offering a "set-it-and-forget-it" experience with an intuitive app. While it provides decent grilling capabilities, particularly for lower-heat cooking, it has limitations regarding high-heat searing due to the lack of direct flames. The grill features a stout build, ample cooking space, and user-friendly design, making it a strong choice for frequent smokers.

title: F5 CEO: AI Is Sparking Cloud Repatriation Movement
summary: F5 CEO François Locoh-Donou states that enterprises are increasingly repatriating application workloads from the cloud due to rising costs and data sovereignty concerns, with AI accelerating this trend. An IDC report suggests 80% of organizations will see some level of repatriation within the next year, indicating a shift towards hybrid and multi-cloud strategies rather than full cloud adoption. This movement creates significant opportunities for partners to help businesses manage and secure applications across diverse environments efficiently.

title: Forever No More. Operator of mall staple Forever 21 files for bankruptcy protection
summary: Forever 21 has filed for bankruptcy protection for a second time, announcing plans to close its U.S. business due to declining mall traffic and aggressive competition from online retailers. F21 OpCo stated it would wind down U.S. operations under Chapter 11, exploring partnership or asset sale options, while international stores continue to operate normally. The company cites competition benefitting from the "de minimis" tax exemption as a significant factor in its inability to find a sustainable path forward.

title: When Facebook Ads Won’t Help Performance Advertisers
summary: This article discusses when Facebook ads are beneficial for performance advertisers and when they may not be. While Facebook offers extensive targeting and can drive traffic, marketers should be aware of diminishing returns due to factors like inappropriate budgets, ad frequency fatigue, rising CPA, and audience demographics. The piece emphasizes the importance of a diversified media mix and exploring alternative advertising channels for sustainable growth.

title: Adobe Analytics: Traffic to U.S. Retail Websites from Generative AI Sources Jumps 1,200 Percent
summary: A new report from Adobe Analytics reveals that traffic to U.S. retail websites from generative AI sources surged by 1,200 percent in February 2025 compared to July 2024, with a 1,300 percent increase during the 2024 holiday season. The study, based on over a trillion retail site visits and a survey of 5,000 U.S. consumers, indicates that 39 percent of consumers use generative AI for online shopping research, product recommendations, and deal seeking. Although conversion rates are slightly lower, AI-driven traffic exhibits 8 percent higher engagement and 12 percent more pages viewed per visit, suggesting AI-assisted shoppers are more informed.

title: Anthropic Enterprise Edge: How Investors Can Gain Exposure Through The AGIX ETF
summary: This article highlights Anthropic's significant position in the AI sector and its ethical approach to AI development. It explains how investors can gain exposure to this private AI company through the KraneShares Artificial Intelligence & Technology ETF (AGIX), which holds Anthropic as its fourth-largest holding. The piece also details Anthropic's rapid growth, strategic partnerships with tech giants like Amazon, Google, Salesforce, and AWS, and the launch of its advanced Claude 3.7 Sonnet AI model.

title: AWS and Accenture to bring cloud skills training to KSA and UAE
summary: AWS and Accenture have partnered to launch the AWS Cloud Institute in Saudi Arabia and the UAE, aiming to address the global shortage of skilled cloud professionals. This initiative utilizes Accenture's LearnVantage platform to deliver comprehensive training and certifications, preparing individuals for careers as cloud developers within approximately nine months. The program includes digital learning, instructor-led sessions, interactive labs, and preparation for AWS certifications, building upon AWS's significant investments in the Middle East.

title: Red Cat Stock Tumbles 7% Ahead of Q3 Earnings – Retail Awaits Contract Updates
summary: Red Cat Holdings (RCAT) shares dropped nearly 7% ahead of its Q3 earnings, with analysts expecting a net loss of $0.09 per share but a 28% year-over-year revenue increase. The decline follows leadership changes, including CEO Jeffrey Thompson serving as interim CFO, and a dip in retail sentiment due to a lack of new contract announcements. Despite this, analysts maintain optimistic long-term price targets, citing potential from new drone contracts and product launches even as the stock has lost over half its value in 2025.

title: Tencent Music has integrated DeepSeek into its streaming service
summary: Tencent Music Entertainment (TME) has integrated DeepSeek, an AI chatbot, into its music streaming service's creation tools, AI assistant, and recommendation pages to enhance user experience. This move comes as TME reported significant Q4 and full-year 2024 earnings, with paid music subscription revenue exceeding $2 billion and gross margins improving. The article also highlights TME's strategy to move beyond price-based competition, scale its own content to reduce royalty costs, and integrate live events for a more comprehensive music experience, despite DeepSeek facing similar ethical questions as other AI in music.

title: Where can investors find defensive assets in today’s evolving markets?
summary: This article explores how investors can identify defensive assets in today's changing market environment, characterized by evolving risks like inflation and varied growth scenarios. T. Rowe Price experts discuss the continued role of the U.S. dollar, the renewed attractiveness of cash due to higher yields, and the changing dynamics of long-maturity U.S. Treasuries. They also touch on the potential defensive qualities of commodities, certain equity sectors like healthcare and consumer staples, and the re-evaluation of the "Magnificent Seven" as a defensive asset class.

title: Adobe Launches Adobe Experience Platform Agent Orchestrator for Businesses to Activate AI Agents in Customer Experiences and Marketing Workflows
summary: Adobe announced the launch of Adobe Experience Platform Agent Orchestrator, designed to help businesses build, manage, and orchestrate AI agents for customer experiences and marketing. The orchestrator includes a suite of ten purpose-built AI agents and introduces Brand Concierge for personalized, conversational brand interactions. Strategic partnerships with major companies like Amazon Web Services and IBM are in place to ensure seamless integration and execution across various AI agent use cases.

title: Adobe Announces New Offerings with AWS and Amazon Ads for Marketers and Creatives to Deliver Impactful Customer Experiences at Scale
summary: Adobe has announced a strategic collaboration with Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Amazon Ads to enhance customer experience orchestration. This partnership aims to provide marketers and creative teams with new tools and integrations, leveraging AWS's cloud services, generative AI, and Amazon Connect, to deliver personalized customer experiences at scale. The offerings include enhanced omnichannel experiences, AI-driven interactions, boosted marketing performance, and streamlined creative workflows through integrations with Adobe Experience Platform, Amazon Marketing Cloud, and Adobe Creative Cloud.

title: Cisco to Deliver Secure AI Infrastructure with NVIDIA
summary: Cisco and NVIDIA are collaborating to create the "Cisco Secure AI Factory with NVIDIA," an architecture designed to simplify and secure the deployment and management of AI infrastructure for enterprises. This initiative integrates networking and security solutions, including Cisco Hypershield and AI Defense, to protect AI workloads, models, and applications. The partnership aims to address complex security challenges in AI factories, offering flexible deployment options with validated reference architectures.

title: INOD Unveils Nvidia-Powered AI Safety Platform: Buy or Hold the Stock?
summary: Innodata (INOD) has launched a new Generative AI Test & Evaluation Platform, powered by Nvidia's inferencing technology, to address AI risk mitigation. While the company has shown impressive financial performance with significant revenue growth and outperforming the market, its stock valuation appears stretched. Investors are advised to exercise caution due to the premium pricing, suggesting a "Hold" recommendation for current shareholders and waiting for a better entry point for new investors.

title: The 4 Best SD Cards of 2026 | Reviews by Wirecutter
summary: This article identifies the best SD cards for various camera needs in 2026, based on extensive testing. The Lexar Professional 1800x V60 UHS-II SDXC is recommended as the top pick for most users due to its speed and affordability, while the SanDisk Extreme V30 UHS-I is the budget option. Special recommendations include the Nextorage A1 Pro for data-intensive Sony cameras and the SanDisk Extreme Pro for cameras using CFexpress Type B.

title: Eschew Magnificent Seven Stock-Picking With This ETF
summary: This article suggests that investors consider actively managed ETFs like the Invesco Top QQQ ETF (QBIG) instead of trying to pick individual Magnificent Seven stocks. The ETF focuses on the Nasdaq-100 Mega Index, which includes the Magnificent Seven plus Broadcom, offering flexibility in the current market. The article highlights that the Magnificent Seven's valuation is at an eight-year low relative to the S&P 500, with companies like Amazon and Alphabet presenting strong potential for growth.

title: Target, Amazon boycotted after DEI rollbacks. Where do NJ corporations stand on DEI?
summary: Consumers are initiating boycotts against major corporations like Target and Amazon following their decisions to roll back Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) policies, with further boycotts planned for other companies like Nestlé, Walmart, General Mills, and McDonald's. The article also examines the DEI policies of South Jersey corporations, specifically detailing the robust DEI commitments made by Campbell's Co. and Subaru of America Inc., both based in Camden. These companies demonstrate their commitment through various initiatives, employee resource groups, and community partnerships.

title: MSCI World ETFs too volatile for you? Three investment alternatives
summary: This article explores alternatives to MSCI World ETFs for investors concerned about their volatility or heavy US stock concentration. It highlights three specific ETF options: MSCI World ex USA, MSCI World Equal Weighted, and MSCI USA ex Mega Cap Select, detailing their compositions and past performance. The piece also advises investors on maintaining a calm approach during market fluctuations, recommending against impulsive selling or excessive buying.

title: Target Corp named second-strongest grocery brand in U.S. for 2025 - Bizwomen
summary: Target Corp. has been recognized as the second-strongest grocery store brand in the U.S. for 2025 by YouGov, based on consumer consideration, ranking only behind Walmart. The company performed particularly well among millennials and was also noted for being the second most improved grocery store in terms of consideration. While grocery is not its primary revenue driver, Target is strategically investing in this segment due to its resilience against economic fluctuations, enhancing offerings like home delivery and supply chain infrastructure.

title: 4 tech giants look cheap ahead of earnings
summary: Ahead of their earnings reports, four major tech companies—Apple, Amazon, Facebook, and Microsoft—are considered undervalued. Analysts see Apple as undervalued despite recent revenue guidance adjustments, Amazon as continuing its impressive growth, Microsoft showing broad-based strength, and Facebook maintaining its competitive advantages in digital advertising despite recent controversies.

title: Rob Arnott on Market Inefficiencies and Investing Opportunities
summary: Rob Arnott, founder of Research Affiliates, discusses market inefficiencies and investing opportunities, focusing on the behavioral mistakes of performance chasing and impatience. He elaborates on the impact of user-friendly AI, the nature of market narratives, and how index investing creates exploitable inefficiencies. Arnott also addresses the growth versus value debate, arguing that value stocks can be as growth-oriented as growth stocks.

title: iRobot made Roomba into an icon. Now, it’s in a huge mess
summary: iRobot, once valued at $4 billion thanks to its iconic Roomba, is now on the brink of insolvency after a failed acquisition by Amazon. The company's decline is attributed to a misguided focus on new product categories while failing to compete with rivals in its core robot vacuum business, leading to plunging revenue and significant losses. iRobot is now attempting a turnaround by refocusing on its core Roomba products with new models featuring advanced technology.

title: Byte-Sized AI: Walmart Announces Gen AI Merchant Tool; Oxford Industries Partners With Exotec
summary: Walmart has launched a new generative AI tool called Wally to help its merchants automate tasks, generate insights, and improve decision-making. Simultaneously, Oxford Industries has partnered with Exotec to implement AI-enabled robotics in its new distribution center, aiming to streamline warehouse operations and returns processing. The article also highlights Augment securing $25 million in funding for its AI-powered logistics assistant, Augie, and Lowe's introducing a gen AI chatbot, Mylow, for home improvement assistance.

title: How AWS opened the floodgates for modern day cloud computing
summary: In 2006, Amazon Web Services (AWS) launched its first service, Amazon S3, pioneering the concept of scalable, cost-effective data storage and effectively creating the cloud computing industry before the term even existed. Initially met with some skepticism, AWS rapidly grew, introducing services like EC2, and distinguishing itself through a first-mover advantage, a "customer-obsession" approach, and consistent price reductions. Today, AWS maintains market leadership but faces new challenges in the AI race, where competitors like Microsoft and Google have made significant investments, prompting AWS to focus on long-term AI innovation and in-house chip development.

title: The 10 best global wide-moat stocks of 2020
summary: This article reviews the top 10 best-performing global wide-moat stocks of 2020, all of which returned over 50%. While none are currently screaming buys, four are fairly valued and make good watchlist candidates. The article provides a brief overview of Veeva Systems, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, Amazon.com, and Tencent Holdings, highlighting their competitive advantages and future growth prospects according to Morningstar analysts.

title: Williams-Sonoma Joins The S&P 500
summary: Williams-Sonoma, Inc. has been added to the S&P 500, a significant milestone for the retailer that acknowledges its brand portfolio and growth strategies. The company's CEO, Laura Alber, stated their commitment to innovation, customer experience, and long-term stakeholder value. This announcement follows a strong fiscal year 2024 finish, with increased net revenue and net earnings in the fourth quarter.

title: Artificial Intelligence at Aflac – Two Use Cases
summary: Aflac, a global leader in supplemental health and life insurance, is leveraging AI to enhance operational security and optimize customer service. The company uses predictive analytics and the CrowdStrike Falcon platform to improve cybersecurity by reducing false positives and accelerating threat detection. Additionally, Aflac employs machine learning and NLP with Pega Platform to automate claim processing and email classification, significantly improving efficiency and customer satisfaction.

title: HIDIVE Expands Service to Amazon Prime Video in U.K., Canada, Australia, New Zealand
summary: AMC Networks announced that its HIDIVE anime streaming service is now available as an ad-free add-on subscription on Amazon Prime Video Channels in the U.K., Canada, Australia, and New Zealand. The direct-to-consumer app is also available in these territories. Additionally, HIDIVE has expanded its availability in the United States through partnerships with Samsung, LG, and VIZIO, and updated its website and apps in March 2024 with new features.

title: Instacart Rolls Out AI-Powered Universal Campaigns for Advertisers
summary: Instacart has launched new AI-powered automation tools, including Universal Campaigns, to help advertisers optimize their ad campaign performance and achieve business goals. Universal Campaigns allow brands to set a single budget and objective, with Instacart's AI automatically managing budget allocation and ad format optimization across various placements like sponsored products and shoppable display ads. These tools aim to simplify campaigning for brands, as demonstrated by early adopters like Rescue Dog Wines and Celsius, who have reported increased customer acquisition and sales.

title: Lands' End's retail cliffhanger - is there time to reverse away from the edge and into an omni-channel future?
summary: Lands' End is exploring strategic alternatives, including a potential sale or merger, as CEO Andrew McLean works to boost e-commerce and personalization despite declining sales. The company has a history of struggling to adapt to the online retail landscape, having been spun off from Sears in 2013, and faces challenges in its physical store presence and partnerships. McLean highlights efforts in marketing, AI-driven personalization, updated websites, and third-party collaborations, while also re-evaluating its traditional catalog strategy as a personalized marketing tool.

title: Is the US Stock Market Cheap Yet?
summary: The US stock market is currently trading at a 5% discount to its fair value, primarily due to significant selloffs in mega-cap technology and AI stocks. While valuations are more attractive than at the start of the year, they haven't reached the deep discounts seen in 2022. Morningstar strategists advise investors to consider overweighting value and small-cap stocks, and to wait for market stabilization before making major moves.

title: Philips and Ibex expand partnership to enhance AI-enabled pathology workflows for better patient care
summary: Philips and Ibex Medical Analytics have expanded their partnership to accelerate the adoption of AI-enabled digital pathology. This collaboration aims to address the shortage of pathologists and the increasing number of cancer patients by enhancing diagnostic accuracy and efficiency through interoperable AI-powered workflows. The new Philips IntelliSite Pathology Solution (PIPS) 6.0 integrates Ibex's AI for improved case prioritization, cancer detection, and reporting, ultimately supporting better patient care.

title: Southern Company: A Hedge Against The Market Which Is Now Just An Income Play (Rating Downgrade)
summary: The author downgrades Southern Company (SO) to neutral, arguing it has become primarily an income play rather than a market hedge, despite benefiting from increased electricity demand. The stock's limited capital appreciation potential and relatively high valuation compared to growth-oriented tech stocks like Amazon, Meta, Google, and Nvidia are cited as reasons for the downgrade. While the dividend remains attractive, the current stock price makes it less appealing for investors seeking capital growth.

title: Tilray Wellness Collaborates with Whole Foods Market to Relaunch Hi*Ball Energy Drinks into National US Retail
summary: Tilray Wellness, a division of Tilray Brands, is re-introducing Hi*Ball Energy drinks into Whole Foods Market stores nationwide after acquiring the brand. Hi*Ball Energy, known for its zero-calorie and zero-sugar formulation, has seen a 68% growth on Amazon in the past six months, prompting its return to brick-and-mortar retail with four best-selling flavors. The collaboration aims to restore the brand's relationship with consumers who previously enjoyed the product.

title: BCX: Examining Inflation Protection Benefits And Recession Risks
summary: The BlackRock Resources & Commodities Strategy Trust (BCX) is a closed-end fund offering commodities exposure and a high income yield, making it attractive for inflation protection. The fund has historically performed well during inflationary periods, outperforming the S&P 500 year-to-date, and trades at a compelling discount to NAV with a significant yield and monthly distributions. While distributions have been fully covered year-to-date, they were not fully covered for the full year 2024.

title: Equities in 2025: Embracing a Broader Landscape
summary: Goldman Sachs Asset Management foresees a broadening landscape of equity market opportunities for active investors in 2025, moving beyond the dominance of US mega-cap tech. The report highlights potential in small-cap companies, developed markets like Japan and Europe, and emerging markets such as India and specific sectors in China. Investors are encouraged to pursue diversified, active strategies and explore long-term themes like reshoring and increased energy demand.

title: Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN) Among the 10 Goldman Sachs Tech Stocks to Buy
summary: Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN) is listed among Goldman Sachs' top 10 tech stocks to buy, despite recent market volatility affecting the tech sector. The company reported strong financial results for 2024, with net sales growing 11% year-over-year, and plans significant capital expenditures in AI and AWS for 2025. Analysts maintain a bullish outlook on AMZN, with a consensus price target suggesting substantial upside potential.

title: Amazon, Tesla and 18 other US companies that bagged maximum H-1B visas in 2024
summary: Amazon and Tesla, along with numerous other US companies, were among the top recipients of H-1B visa approvals in 2025, according to USCIS data. Amazon led with 9,265 approvals, followed by Cognizant and Google, while Indian IT giants like Infosys and TCS also secured a significant number of visas. These companies rely heavily on skilled foreign workers for specialized roles in technology, engineering, research, and development.

title: Google's $32B Deal Fuels Cybersecurity Boom: Bet on OKTA, FTNT Stocks
summary: Google's $32 billion acquisition of cloud security firm Wiz signals a major shift in the cybersecurity landscape, highlighting the increasing importance of cloud and AI security. This deal positions cybersecurity companies like Okta (OKTA) and Fortinet (FTNT) for significant growth, as demand for identity security and AI-driven network protection rises. Both companies are rated Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), making them compelling investment opportunities amidst this industry boom.

title: Commanders' owner Josh Harris makes another impressive hire
summary: The Washington Commanders, under owner Josh Harris, have hired Andy VanHorn, a principal developer of Amazon's second headquarters, to lead the team's new stadium project. VanHorn, formerly of JBG Smith Properties, brings extensive experience in mixed-use development, including significant projects like Amazon HQ2 and Virginia Tech's innovation campus. This move highlights Harris's strategic approach to the franchise's real estate needs, contrasting with the previous ownership's handling of the stadium search.

title: Which High-Yield Dividend ETF Is the Safest To Buy Now: JPMorgan's JEPI vs. Vanguard's VYMI
summary: This article compares the JPMorgan Equity Premium Income ETF (JEPI) and the Vanguard International High Dividend Yield ETF (VYMI) to determine which offers greater safety for high-yield dividend investors. While JEPI boasts a higher dividend yield and trading volume, VYMI provides broader geographic diversification and a larger number of component stocks. The article concludes that VYMI might be safer for investors prioritizing geographic diversification despite JEPI's higher yield.

title: Can Nuclear Energy Help Big Tech Meet Data Center Needs?
summary: The growing electricity demands of data centers, particularly due to AI, are leading Big Tech companies to consider nuclear energy, including small modular reactors (SMRs). While wind and solar are carbon-free, they don't provide the consistent power required, and natural gas, though quick and cheap, has carbon emissions. However, SMRs are expensive and take a long time to come online, posing challenges for utilities trying to meet this new demand while managing costs and timelines.

title: H&R Block hires former Amazon Web Services cybersecurity exec to protect its data
summary: H&R Block has hired a new chief information security officer, formerly an Amazon Web Services cybersecurity executive, to bolster its defenses against cyber threats. This move comes as the company has faced previous challenges, including a data breach and litigation. The new hire is expected to enhance the protection of H&R Block's sensitive data.

title: 27 Kohl's stores are set to close Saturday. See list of the closures in 15 states
summary: Kohl's is closing 27 "underperforming" store locations across 15 states on Saturday, March 29. These closures are part of a larger transformation initiative, which includes corporate workforce reductions and changes in e-commerce operations, following declines in sales for 2024. Despite these closures, Kohl's will still operate over 1,120 stores nationwide.

title: AT&T In Talks To Buy Lumen Technologies’ Consumer Fiber Unit Amid Lumen’s AI Push: Report
summary: AT&T is reportedly in discussions to acquire Lumen Technologies’ consumer fiber operations, a deal that could be valued at over $5.5 billion. This potential sale aligns with Lumen's strategy to divest non-profitable business units and focus on its enterprise services, particularly in building infrastructure for AI, which now accounts for 75 percent of its revenue. Lumen's CEO, Kate Johnson, has emphasized growing the company by providing the backbone for AI, recently securing $8.5 billion in private connectivity deals.

title: Nuclear startup Terrestrial Energy goes public via SPAC, netting $280M in merger
summary: Terrestrial Energy, a nuclear startup based in North Carolina, has merged with a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC), raising $280 million. The company, which develops integral molten salt reactors (IMSRs), plans to list on Nasdaq under the symbol IMSR. This move follows the increasing interest in nuclear power as a solution to rising electricity demand, particularly from data centers and AI operations.

title: EJH Share Surge: An Unexpected Upside?
summary: E-Home Household Service Holdings Limited (NASDAQ: EJH) saw its stock surge 16.18% on Wednesday, reportedly due to a new partnership announcement in the home services sector. The article details EJH's financial performance, including a closing price of 1.185, a Price-to-Sales ratio of 0.13, and significant total assets with no massive debts. Investors are debating whether this uptick is a fleeting rally or a strategic opportunity, with analysts emphasizing careful evaluation over hasty decisions.

title: Akamai distributes AI inference across the globe, promising lower latency and higher throughput
summary: Akamai Technologies Inc. has launched Akamai Cloud Inference, a new service designed to distribute AI inference closer to users globally, leveraging its highly distributed cloud infrastructure. This aims to reduce latency and increase throughput for AI models, particularly for the operational phase of AI, by moving inference from centralized cloud platforms to the edge. Akamai Cloud Inference offers compute resources including CPUs, GPUs, and ASICs, integrates with Nvidia's AI Enterprise software and Vast Data for advanced data management, and supports containerized workloads and edge compute capabilities.

title: CoreWeave prices IPO lower than expected, and its stock still sags on its debut before recovering
summary: CoreWeave Inc.'s stock experienced a volatile debut, initially falling over 5% despite pricing its IPO lower than anticipated at $40, but later recovered to close 2.5% above its initial trade price. The cloud computing infrastructure company, which raised $1.5 billion, faced investor concerns regarding its reliance on two major customers, significant debt, and the capital-intensive nature of its business model. Despite attracting Nvidia as a major backer, many investors questioned CoreWeave's long-term sustainability and the broader macroeconomic climate's impact on IPO appetite.

title: What is the dividend yield of the iShares S&P 500 ETF (IVV)?
summary: The article discusses the dividend yield of the iShares S&P 500 ETF (IVV), noting its excellent capital returns over the past five years driven by US tech giants, despite a relatively low dividend yield of 1.01% as of February 2025. It emphasizes that while IVV isn't ideal for large investment income, its overall net return and low management fee make it attractive for long-term growth due to its exposure to strong US businesses benefiting from trends like digitalization and AI.

title: Amazon Autos wants to sell used cars—here’s what it can’t screw up
summary: Amazon Autos is planning to expand its platform to include used car sales, building on its existing partnership with Hyundai for new car sales. The article highlights three critical non-negotiables for Amazon to succeed in this venture while aligning customer experience with dealer profitability: preserving dealer F&I profits, reinforcing the value of used car listings beyond just price, and minimizing dealer exposure to return policies. The success hinges on Amazon understanding and supporting the complex mechanics that make used car retailing profitable for dealerships.

title: JBG Looks To Sell Union Market Apartment Building For $180M
summary: JBG Smith is reportedly selling The Batley, a 432-unit apartment building in Washington D.C.'s Union Market, for $180M, which is a significant discount from its $205M purchase price in 2021. The REIT indicated it no longer wishes to own the property and has been on a selling spree recently, experiencing a substantial net loss in the fourth quarter. Residents have been informed of their Tenant Opportunity to Purchase Act rights.

title: CoreWeave Stock Treads Water After Scaled-Back IPO
summary: CoreWeave, an AI-focused cloud computing company, had a lukewarm IPO, with its stock ending the day at its IPO price of $40 per share, despite initial stumbling. The scaled-back IPO and initial trading performance raise questions about investor appetite for AI stocks amidst a broader tech slump and concerns about CoreWeave's concentrated sales and significant debt. The company's debut is seen as a litmus test for the AI market after Nvidia's recent decline.

title: Gartner: The top supply chain technology trends for 2025 are…
summary: Gartner has identified seven key technology trends that will significantly influence supply chain organizations in 2025, driven by the overarching themes of enhanced connectivity and intelligence. These trends include ambient invisible intelligence, augmented connected workforce, multimodal user interfaces, polyfunctional robots, agentic AI, autonomous data collection, intelligent simulation, and decision intelligence. The goal is to improve operational efficiency, adaptability, and facilitate competitive differentiation.

title: PLDT Strengthens Digital Growth with Data Center Expansion
summary: PLDT is heavily investing in data center expansion as a core part of its digital growth strategy in Southeast Asia. Through its subsidiary ePLDT, the company operates a network of VITRO data centers, including the largest in the Philippines, VITRO Sta. Rosa, which is set to become the nation's AI hub. PLDT is also preparing for an AI-powered future by offering GPU-as-a-Service, further solidifying its leadership in digital transformation.

summary: This article highlights 12 leading companies, including Alice & Bob, Amazon, D-Wave Systems, and Google, that are actively developing quantum computing hardware and software. The article also discusses the potential impact of quantum computing on various industries and the challenges that still need to be overcome.

The report details the company's financial performance, including revenue and profitability, and showcases impactful campaigns for major brands. WPP also made strides in non-financial indicators like increasing women in executive leadership and expanding WPP Open monthly active users.

summary: Amazon is holding its "Smile SALE: New Life FINAL" until April 1, 2025, offering discounts on over a million items including AI gadgets. Featured products include the PLAUD NOTE voice recorder with AI transcription, various Amazfit smartwatches (Active 2, Balance with GPT-4o, and T-Rex 3), Dangbei projectors (Atom and DBOX02), and 1MORE audio products (SonoFlow Pro HQ51 headphones and Open Earbuds S51). summary: STAG Industrial (STAG) is recommended as a buy due to its strong fundamentals, consistent dividend history, and resilience in a challenging interest rate environment for REITs. The company's diversified portfolio of 591 buildings, including key tenants like Amazon, ensures stable and reliable income. Despite a modest dividend increase, STAG's robust coverage rate and long history of payouts make it an attractive option for long-term income, with Wall Street analysts projecting potential for double-digit returns.

summary: This article discusses the transformative impact of "AI²" — artificial intelligence (AI) and artificial incretins (GLP-1s) — on the technology and healthcare sectors. title: The 12 Best Pellet Grills, According To Reviews

title: OpenAI closes $40 billion funding round, largest private tech deal on record
summary: OpenAI has secured a record-setting $40 billion funding round, valuing the company at $300 billion, including the new capital. This makes it the largest private tech deal ever, with SoftBank contributing $30 billion and a syndicate of investors, including Microsoft, making up the rest.
